Tim Benjamin is confident he can stand up to the physical challenge as he bids to make the final of the 400 metres at the World Championships following a season severely affected by illness and injury.
Tim Benjamin is Britain’s leading 400m man and will also compete in the 4x400m relay; he’s in great form having recently handed the Olympic Champion a rare defeat (see below).

Tim Benjamin was the favourite in the 400 metres in spite of missing much pre-season conditioning, suffering a cold in the run up to the event and facing up to a Woodford Green onslaught in the form of Davis and Hedman.
6-14 IAAF 10th World Championships, Helsinki FIN. 400m: (12) 5 T Benjamin 44.93 (3s2 (10) 45.66, 1h1 (09) 44.85). 800m: 7h3 (11) P Owor 1:51.72.

Tim Benjamin is glad his summer season has finally come to an end despite the success he has enjoyed over 400metres. Benjamin was runner-up to Tyree Washington in a thrilling one-lap encounter in Monaco and his time capped an outstanding couple of months.
The win saw him become the second British champion over the distance, following in the footsteps of 1999 winner Tim Benjamin who is now carving out an international career over 400 metres.

Finally, and most excitingly, in Tim Benjamin we could have the next big thing in British athletics.
